name: wumpus
desc: Exact clone of the ancient BASIC Hunt the Wumpus game
why: An exact clone of the original BASIC Hunt the Wumpus, a classic and strange piece of computing history.

brief.what_it_is: Wumpus is a command-line clone of the old BASIC game Hunt the Wumpus, reproduced exactly, including its clumsy user interface. The installed command is 'wumpus', and the package also ships a second executable, 'superhack', which the author describes as a satire that is structurally similar to Wumpus. The pages do not describe the input format or the play mechanics in detail, so the game itself is not described here beyond being a faithful transcription. Output is the game's text on the terminal.
brief.why_it_exists: The author, Eric S. Raymond, wrote it as retrocomputing nostalgia: 'WUMPUS is a bit of retrocomputing nostalgia. It is an exact clone, even down to the godawful user interface, of an ancient classic game.' It also preserves the original Gregory Yob game from 1973, which the README calls the first exploration game to use a non-grid worldmap.
brief.how_it_works: The project is a clone made by transcribing the original BASIC source, which the README says is included in comments in the code. The README says the version fixes two minor bugs in the author's original USENET posting of the source. The pages do not describe the internals further.

commands_seen.context: Synopsis line from the wumpus(6) man page; runs the Hunt the Wumpus game.

brief.install_notes: The homepage offers a gzipped source tarball (wumpus-1.12.tar.gz) and the project is usually packaged as 'wumpus'. The recent change noted is 'Repair Makefile errors', so the build is a plain make-based source build. No hardware, accounts, or runtime setup is mentioned. The Homebrew formula's executables are 'superhack' and 'wumpus'.
brief.standout: It is a deliberately exact clone, bugs and bad interface included, of a 1970s game that the README credits as the first exploration game to use a non-grid map, predating Colossal Cave Adventure. The bundled satire, superhack, is a second game in the same package.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage is dated 04 Apr 2026 and lists version 1.12 with a recent 'Repair Makefile errors' change. The README was last updated 2026-01-29 and the man page 2026-02-18.
brief.caveats: Dates in the sources disagree slightly: the README says Yob wrote the game in 1973 and that the BASIC source was probably close to its 1975 publication in Creative Computing, while the man page says the Atari game is from 1974. The README notes one historical liberty: the project logo comes from a later TI-99/4A version with a graphical interface. The README warns nothing about platform or licensing beyond a COPYING file (license not read). The homepage asks readers to support the author on Patreon, and the page lists donors.

entry.title: Wumpus
entry.tldr: An exact clone of Gregory Yob's 1973 Hunt the Wumpus, bad interface included, plus a bundled satire called superhack.
entry.deeper_look:
Wumpus is a command-line reproduction of the old BASIC game Hunt the Wumpus. Eric S. Raymond made it by transcribing the original BASIC source, which the README says is kept in comments in the code. The README says this version fixes two minor bugs from his original USENET posting of the source. It is meant to be faithful, not improved.

The author's own description: "WUMPUS is a bit of retrocomputing nostalgia. It is an *exact* clone, even down to the godawful user interface, of an ancient classic game." Expect text prompts, not a modern game UI. The pages read for this entry do not spell out the input format or the rules, so start the game and see what it asks you.

The idea underneath is historical. The README credits Gregory Yob's game as the first exploration game to use a non-grid world map, and it predates Colossal Cave Adventure. Playing it shows what a game looked like when the map was a graph of connected rooms rather than a grid, and when a few lines of BASIC were the whole program.

The package also installs a second executable, superhack. The README describes it as "a satire, structurally quite similar to WUMPUS."

try_this.what_happens: Starts Hunt the Wumpus in the terminal, with the original game's text interface.
Runs the bundled satire, which the README says is structurally similar to Wumpus.
Asks the program for usage information, if it provides any.

entry.whats_unique: It is a deliberately exact transcription of a 1970s original, flaws and all, with the BASIC source preserved in the code comments. It also ships a satirical second game.
entry.caveats: The interface is intentionally clumsy, and the sources disagree slightly on dates: the README says 1973, while the man page says the Atari game is from 1974.
